anchor.quote: Let $r$ be the ring degree: the number of complex coefficients in each element, a power of two.

anchor.note: Complex numbers are a known concept in the reader profile (undergraduate computer science: complex numbers), so the complex coefficient field C is covered.

gaps.note: The reader knows quotient rings and basic ring notions, but ideals and ideal generation are abstract algebra beyond basics; the page neither explains nor links them, so the 'Equivalently' identification with the quotient C[y]/(y^r+1) cannot be checked.

gaps.quote: the coefficient ring in which the root multiplications of the remaining axes become cheap shifts
gaps.note: The page never says what the remaining axes are or why their root multiplications become shifts in this ring; the claim is not derivable from the page.

gaps.term: cited claim on powers of y
gaps.quote: Powers of $y$ (cited), and each such root acts on a coefficient list as a signed shift.
gaps.note: The page does not state what the cited source establishes about powers of y, so the reader cannot tell what is being attributed; the link from the cited claim to the page's own signed-shift behaviour is not stated.

gaps.quote: therefore needs only signed shifts, rearrangements of addresses, and additions and subtractions
gaps.note: No transform over this ring is defined on the page, so the reader cannot check from the page that a transform whose roots are powers of y uses only these operations.
